html:
The Chowanoke were an Algonquian-speaking people of the Chowan River in northeastern North Carolina. When the English arrived in the 1580s they were the largest and most powerful people of the region.

In 1586 Ralph Lane, leader of the first Roanoke colony, went up the Chowan and met their chief Menatonon, who told him of copper and of lands to the west. The Chowanoke stayed strong through the mid 1600s, but as English settlers spread south from Virginia they fought back and lost a war in 1677. They were then confined to a small reservation, which they slowly lost through debts and land sales in the 1700s.

Their neighbours included the Weapemeoc to the east and the Iroquoian Tuscarora and Meherrin to the west. A Chowanoke tribe reorganised in the 2000s.
